title: 39 patcher tests fail at HEAD: harness exports DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE pointing at a nonexistent stage
description:
39 patcher tests fail at HEAD (6de7a320). Regression introduced by eseq-linux.36's
eseq-side change; the upstream artifact work in .36 is correct and verified.

REPRODUCE (no env, clean shell):
  cargo test -q -p eseqlisp --lib -- widget_render::patcher::tests::
  -> 450 passed; 39 failed

  fatal error: 'dgen_runtime.h' file not found

CAUSE. 6de7a320 added to compile_patch_source_with_dgenlisp (patcher/tests.rs:1868):
    let runtime_include = patcher_test_dgen_toolchain_root(repo_root).join("include");
    ... .env("DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE", runtime_include)
        .arg("--skip-inline-audit")
and patcher_test_dgen_toolchain_root (:1850) resolves:
    ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT, else repo_root/crates/sequencer/tools/dgen-toolchain

crates/sequencer/tools/dgen-toolchain DOES NOT EXIST in this tree -- it is the
gitignored ~147 MB stage that has never been produced for Linux (eseq-linux.30),
and ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT is unset in a normal shell. So the harness now
exports DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE pointing at a nonexistent directory.

WHY THIS IS PARTICULARLY UNFORTUNATE: setting that variable to a bad path
OVERRIDES the executable-relative resolution that eseq-linux.36 just added
upstream. Verified independently -- the published v0.1.1 tar.gz
(sha256 717b5cb6..., matches content/dgenlisp.lock) extracts to a self-contained
tree carrying toolchain/include, toolchain/abi and scripts/audit-dgen-elf-so.sh,
and compiles a patch to .c/.json/.so with NO env vars set, from an unrelated
working directory, glibc floor 2.35. The binary no longer needs the hint; the
hint is what breaks it.

Note the tests currently exec crates/sequencer/tools/DGenLisp-linux-x86_64 (the
old in-place Arch build, sha 53c4cd54...), which is NOT self-sufficient -- which
is presumably why the env var was added. But the path it points at is wrong.
Note also that CLAUDE.md's cheap clean-HEAD recipe exports the SAME nonexistent
path, so it will not rescue this either.

FIX OPTIONS -- prefer the one that removes the special case:
 A. Have the harness use the fetched, self-contained v0.1.1 distribution and set
    NO DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE at all. Cleanest, and it is what eseq-linux.35 is
    building anyway. Coordinate rather than duplicating.
 B. If an override is kept, only export it when the directory actually EXISTS,
    and fail with a clear message naming the missing stage otherwise. Silently
    exporting a bad path is what turned a resolvable situation into 39 red tests.
 C. Do not simply set ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT in developer shells and call it
    fixed -- that reproduces the works-on-my-machine pattern this chain has
    already removed twice.

Keep --skip-inline-audit; that part is right (eseq audits dylibs itself via
lisp_host/dgen/dgen_audit.rs).
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p eseqlisp --lib -- widget_render::patcher::tests:: passes with NO environment variables set in a clean shell; the harness never exports DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE pointing at a path that does not exist; if a stage override is retained it is applied only when present and produces an actionable error when absent; --skip-inline-audit is retained; the fix is coordinated with eseq-linux.35 rather than duplicating its fetch logic
notes:
FIXED with option A (lock-driven, self-contained distribution; NO DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE).

WHY A, not B: acceptance requires a green suite in a clean shell. Option B (export
the override only when the stage exists) would leave the tests running the vendored
crates/sequencer/tools/DGenLisp-linux-x86_64, sha 53c4cd54..., which is the old
in-place Arch build. It only resolves its headers because /home/alec/code/dgen-audio
was baked into it at build time, so B would be green on this machine and red
everywhere else -- the works-on-my-machine pattern option C warns about. Nothing in
the tree provides a real include dir to point an override at.

CHANGE (crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/patcher/tests.rs only, +269/-35):
- Removed patcher_test_dgen_toolchain_root and the DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE export.
  The published distribution resolves headers/abi/audit scripts relative to its own
  executable; the hint is what defeated that.
- Removed DGENLISP_TOOL_FILENAME; added DGENLISP_LOCK_TARGET (macos-arm64 /
  linux-x86_64 / None) and a small content/dgenlisp.lock stanza parser.
- patcher_test_install_dgenlisp: resolve the pinned artifact into
  $CARGO_TARGET_DIR/dgenlisp/<version>/ (else <repo>/target/dgenlisp/<version>/),
  guarded by a .dgenlisp-sha256 stamp. Cold cache -> curl the pinned url, verify
  sha256 against the lock as a hard error, extract (tar.gz) or install (executable)
  into a staging dir, chmod +x, then rename into place atomically.
  A tracked format=executable artifact whose sha256 already matches the pin is used
  in place, so macOS keeps using crates/sequencer/tools/DGenLisp-macos-arm64
  (f58b2abc..., which does match the lock) with no network.
- patcher_test_dgenlisp_tool keeps the ESEQ_DGENLISP_TOOL escape hatch and wraps the
  installer in a OnceLock so the 38 parallel dgen tests install exactly once.
- --skip-inline-audit retained, with a comment pointing at
  crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/dgen/dgen_audit.rs.

OVERLAP WITH eseq-linux.35: this installer is deliberately minimal and lives only in
the test harness; a doc comment says so and names .35. .35 should delete it and route
the harness through the product-wide fetcher. No .gitignore change was needed
(target/ is already ignored) and no vendored binary or lock file was touched.

VERIFIED, clean shell (env -i, only HOME/PATH/TERM; no ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT,
DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE or ESEQ_DGENLISP_TOOL):

  $ cargo test -q -p eseqlisp --lib -- widget_render::patcher::tests::
  test result: FAILED. 488 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 1206 filtered out

All 38 dgen_runtime.h failures are gone. The single remaining failure,
patcher_alignment_snaps_dragged_output_to_other_input_x, is pre-existing and
unrelated -- confirmed failing at HEAD 6de7a320 in a detached worktree -- and is
filed as eseq-linux.38.

Also verified: the fetch really runs (target/dgenlisp/dgenlisp-v0.1.1/ holds the
extracted 62 MB tree with DGenLisp, toolchain/include, toolchain/abi and
scripts/audit-dgen-elf-so.sh, stamped 717b5cb6...), and deleting the stamp triggers a
correct re-download and rename over the existing install. rustfmt- and clippy-clean
over the new lines.

NOT COMMITTED, NOT PUSHED (branch carries the 62 MB blob in ed326340, eseq-linux.34).
Also filed eseq-linux.39 for the unsound CLAUDE.md clean-HEAD recipe.

title: Excise the 62 MB DGenLisp blob from unpushed history before the branch is pushed
description:
TIME-SENSITIVE. Verified 2026-08-23: the 62 MB binary blob exists ONLY in local
unpushed commits. Once it is pushed it is permanent for every clone, forever.

  git rev-list --objects origin/eseq-linux | grep -c DGenLisp-linux-x86_64
  -> 0        (not yet on the remote)

  unpushed:  bd97de3d  Resolve DGenLisp compiler per target
             ed326340  build(dgen): vendor per-target compiler binaries   <-- the blob
             995491f7  feat(eseqlisp): add deterministic text capture harness

CONTEXT: the user reversed the tracked-binary decision on 2026-08-23 after seeing
the numbers -- 62 MB compressed per re-vendor (binaries barely compress: 64 MB on
disk -> 62 MB in git), against a .git that is currently 191 MB total, with an
expected update cadence of WEEKLY OR MORE. At that cadence a tracked blob adds
roughly 3 GB per year. Vendoring moves to publish-and-fetch-by-lock; see the
sibling beads.

CONFLICT TO RESOLVE BEFORE ACTING -- READ THIS:
The eseq-linux branch must be pushed for eseq-linux.24 (the macOS glyph capture)
to happen at all; that handoff is 'worker pushes, user pulls on the Mac'. If the
branch is pushed before this bead lands, the 62 MB becomes permanent and this bead
becomes a much uglier shared-history rewrite. So either this lands first, or the
Mac handoff is done from a branch that does not carry ed326340. Do not push
eseq-linux with ed326340 intact.

WORK:
 1. Rewrite the unpushed commits so no DGenLisp binary blob is ever introduced.
    ed326340 is the only commit that adds one. Simplest correct shape: rewrite
    ed326340 to keep its non-binary content (the rebuild_dgenlisp_tool.sh changes
    and the path/layout intent) and drop both binary files, leaving bd97de3d's
    consumer resolution pointing at fetched, gitignored paths.
 2. This MUST be sequenced with the fetch mechanism. Removing the binaries without
    a way to obtain them leaves the tree broken exactly as it was between .15 and
    .14 -- AppPaths resolving to files that do not exist. Land the fetch bead
    first, or land both together.
 3. Confirm afterwards with:
      git rev-list --objects --all | grep DGenLisp-  # no binary paths
      du -sh .git                                    # should drop well below 191 MB
 4. Keep the macOS binary out too. It is only 4.1 MB, but a split scheme where one
    target is tracked and the other fetched is the asymmetry the user already
    rejected once.

NOTE: git gc / repack may be needed for .git to actually shrink after the rewrite;
the blob lingers in reflog and packs until pruned.
acceptance_criteria: git rev-list --objects --all shows no DGenLisp binary paths; .git size is materially below 191 MB after gc/prune; the working tree still resolves both DGenLisp targets via the fetch mechanism and the previously-failing patcher tests still pass on Linux; ed326340's non-binary content (rebuild script changes) is preserved; nothing was force-pushed over shared history -- the rewrite happened while the commits were still local, or the user explicitly approved a shared rewrite
close_reason: Rewrote the 8 unpushed commits: ed326340 amended to keep only rebuild_dgenlisp_tool.sh changes + old DGenLisp deletion (now 443a779f); both 62MB linux and 4.2MB macos-arm64 blobs never enter history. Final tree byte-identical to old tip. Reflog expired + gc: .git 181M->150M, zero DGenLisp-<target> objects under --all. Branch fast-forwards from origin/eseq-linux; no shared history touched. Fetch script resolves lock; 489/489 patcher tests pass. Note: pre-existing 4.2MB tools/DGenLisp blobs in already-pushed shared history remain (removing them would require the forbidden shared rewrite).

title: patcher_alignment_snaps_dragged_output_to_other_input_x fails on Linux
description:
Pre-existing failure on Linux, independent of the DGenLisp harness work in eseq-linux.37.

REPRODUCE (clean shell, no env):
  cargo test -q -p eseqlisp --lib -- widget_render::patcher::tests::patcher_alignment_snaps_dragged_output_to_other_input_x

  panicked at crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/patcher/tests.rs (assert on `aligned`):
  (0.0, 10.0)

Confirmed failing at HEAD 6de7a320 in a detached worktree, so it is NOT a regression
from .37. It was one of the 39 red tests reported in .37; the other 38 were the
dgen_runtime.h failures and are now green.

The test primes text metrics (prime_patcher_text_metrics) and expects
align_dragged_primary_position to snap x to 0.5; on Linux it returns the input
position unchanged and snap.snapped_x is presumably false. Node widths are
explicitly set (12.0 / 20.0), but port x positions are derived from measured text,
so this most likely tracks the Linux font-fallback / glyph-metrics work
(eseq-linux.18 and the fontdue atlas replacement) producing different advance
widths than the CoreText path the expectation was authored against.

Decide whether the expectation is font-dependent and should be made metric-agnostic,
or whether Linux text metrics are actually wrong.
acceptance_criteria: The test passes on Linux in a clean shell, and the fix makes clear whether the expectation was font-dependent or the Linux metrics were wrong.

title: Published DGenLisp asset has container /src paths baked in; cannot compile standalone
description:
The dgenlisp-v0.1.0 Linux release asset has the CONTAINER'S mount path baked in as
its dgen-checkout root, so it cannot compile a patch on any machine. Found
2026-08-23 by downloading the published asset and running it standalone.

WHAT PASSES: the artifact is otherwise correct. glibc floor 2.35 (verified via
objdump on the downloaded file), ldd clean -- only libc/libm/libstdc++/libgcc_s/
loader, no libswift*/libFoundation*/lib_FoundationICU. sha256
9cd9954fc477c81188f76f7aea499e4d50a3e96b876c6c55daae2e982cea55b2, 64249592 bytes.
Repo is public and unauthenticated download returns 200. eseq-linux.33's container
work was right; this is a separate leak it did not check for.

THE DEFECT -- TWO BAKED /src PATHS, both from `-v /home/alec/code/dgen-audio:/src`:

  1. runtime header root
       $ DGenLisp compile t.lisp -o out --name s --sample-rate 44100 --voices 12
       Compilation error: clang failed: 'dgen_runtime.h' file not found
     The binary looks for toolchain/include under its build-time source root,
     i.e. /src/toolchain/include, which exists only inside the container.

  2. inline audit script -- surfaces only after fixing (1)
       DGen binary audit script not found: /src/scripts/audit-dgen-elf-so.sh.
       This default is the build machine's dgen checkout and does not exist here.

PROOF IT IS THE BINARY, NOT THE ENVIRONMENT (both run with identical cwd):
  old Arch-built binary, run from /tmp scratchpad  -> emits .c + .json + .so  OK
  new published binary, run from eseq tools/       -> emits .c only           FAIL
The old one only ever worked by accident: it was built in place at
/home/alec/code/dgen-audio/.build, so its baked checkout root happens to exist on
Alec's machine. It would fail the same way on any other machine. The container
build did not introduce this class of bug, it exposed it.

WORKAROUND CONFIRMED TO PROGRESS THE BUILD:
  DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE=<dgen-audio>/toolchain/include  ->  gets past (1), emits .so
  then --skip-inline-audit or --audit-tool <path>       ->  needed for (2)
DGenLisp already documents all of these in --help: --toolchain-root,
--audit-tool (overrides DGEN_BINARY_AUDIT_TOOL and the dgen-checkout fallback),
and --skip-inline-audit ("the host process audits the artifact itself").

WORK -- pick the upstream fix, and land the eseq-side guard regardless:
 A. UPSTREAM (correct fix, in dgen-audio): resolve the runtime include dir and
    the audit script relative to the EXECUTABLE, or from an explicit env/flag, and
    fail with a clear message when unset -- never from a build-time absolute path.
    A relocatable compiler is the actual requirement for a published artifact.
    Republish as v0.1.1 and update the lock.
 B. ESEQ SIDE (eseq-linux.35 must do this even if A lands): never invoke DGenLisp
    bare. Always pass the include root and either --skip-inline-audit (eseq already
    audits dylibs itself -- see lisp_host/dgen/dgen_audit.rs) or an explicit
    --audit-tool. eseq already has ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT plumbing to hang this on.

LANDMINE FOR eseq-linux.35: eseq's patcher tests pass RIGHT NOW only because
crates/sequencer/tools/DGenLisp-linux-x86_64 is still the old in-place Arch build
(sha 53c4cd54...). The moment .35 swaps to the fetched artifact those 38 tests go
red again unless the include root and audit flags are wired first. Do not treat a
green suite today as evidence the fetched binary works.

ALSO NOTED while reading the binary's strings, unrelated but worth a bead if it
bites: DGenLisp requires x86-64-v3 (AVX2 + FMA, Haswell/Zen1+) and warns that
below it every FMA silently double-rounds and the .so traps with SIGILL on the
audio thread; DGEN_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_HOST_CPU=1 overrides. Relevant to CI runner
selection in eseq-linux.32.
design:
KEEP THE DOCKER CONTAINER BUILD. eseq-linux.33's container work is correct and must not be reverted while fixing this -- swift:6.3.3-jammy is what produces the glibc 2.35 floor, verified on the published asset, and building on the Arch host is what caused the GLIBC_2.44 regression this chain already fixed once.

Distinguish the two compilations, which this bug straddles:
  (1) building the DGenLisp executable itself, Swift -> binary. Happens in the
      Ubuntu container, once per re-vendor. This is where the /src paths leak in.
  (2) DGenLisp compiling a user patch, .lisp -> .c -> .so. Happens natively on
      every consumer machine, on every instrument edit, using that machine's
      clang (or the hermetic stage per eseq-linux.30).
The defect is introduced in (1) and only manifests in (2). Fixing it means
stopping (1) from baking its build-time source root into (2)'s defaults -- not
abandoning the container.

DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY MATCHING THE MOUNT PATH. Mounting the repo at
-v /home/alec/code/dgen-audio:/home/alec/code/dgen-audio would make the baked
path resolve on Alec's Surface and nowhere else, reproducing exactly the
build-on-my-machine failure mode this chain has now eliminated twice (Swift
runtime linkage, then glibc floor). A published artifact must be relocatable.
acceptance_criteria: The published Linux asset compiles a patch to .c + .json + .so from an arbitrary working directory on a machine with no dgen-audio checkout, with no /src path referenced in any error; the fix is either upstream relocatability (republished as a new tag with content/dgenlisp.lock updated) or explicit eseq-side flags, and which was chosen is recorded; eseq's 38 patcher tests pass against the FETCHED binary, not the old in-place one; no error message references a build-machine path
notes: Completed upstream relocatability and retained the eseq-side guard. dgen-audio commit ae25e9d9913ac745c653b6c7df4236b1a42b32f8 removes all #filePath checkout fallbacks: runtime headers and audit scripts now resolve relative to the executable, explicit DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE/--audit-tool overrides still win, and missing resources fail with actionable paths that contain no build-machine checkout. Three focused upstream tests pass. The commit is pushed on linux-c-backend. Rebuilt in swift:6.3.3-jammy with the required /src mount, /src/.build-container scratch path, static Swift stdlib, and non-root UID. The verbatim command was attempted first but SwiftPM failed writing /.cache for the unmapped non-root UID; the successful rerun added only -e HOME=/tmp, preserving the exact image, /src mount, workdir, build flags, and glibc provenance. Stripped Linux binary sha256 cb986ab57d1b0b7b50e938e05915ca71ef1d9d95ed12483fc39a9d60843e3060, 64249592 bytes, maximum GLIBC_2.35; ldd only libc/libm/libstdc++/libgcc_s/loader. Published dgenlisp-v0.1.1 with a standalone tar distribution sha256 717b5cb629928459d8b366d5b75afabe46800c70639a0de3fb0fb29246c2ff61. Independently downloaded that archive into /tmp with no checkout in scope; bare compile emitted nonempty .c/.json/.so, inline ELF audit passed, and no /src path appeared. content/dgenlisp.lock pins the v0.1.1 Linux archive and retains the v0.1.0 macOS binary. Eseq commit 6de7a320 adds the lock and makes the patcher harness explicitly pass DGEN_RUNTIME_INCLUDE plus --skip-inline-audit. All 37 current DGenLisp-backed patcher tests passed against the separately downloaded v0.1.1 bare binary (the bead's count of 38 is stale).
close_reason: Made DGenLisp resources executable-relative upstream, rebuilt and published v0.1.1 from the Jammy container at GLIBC_2.35, pinned the standalone archive, and verified all current fetched-binary patcher tests.

title: Fetch DGenLisp by lock file instead of tracking binaries (eseq side)
description:
eseq side of the vendoring reversal (user decision, 2026-08-23): stop tracking
DGenLisp binaries; commit a lock file and fetch the pinned artifact on demand.

WHY: 62 MB compressed per Linux re-vendor, expected update cadence weekly or more,
against a 191 MB .git. Tracking does not survive that at any binary size. The
publish-and-fetch shape keeps repo growth at zero per update while preserving the
property the user cares about -- a contributor needs neither a Swift toolchain nor
the dgen-audio checkout.

PRECONDITION: the upstream publish bead must land first; this bead consumes the
artifacts it produces.

title: Build and publish per-target DGenLisp release artifacts from an old-glibc container
description:
Build the Linux DGenLisp in a Docker container on Alec's Arch box, and publish
both per-target binaries as GitHub release assets on dgen-audio. Nothing built
by this bead gets committed into eseq -- eseq-linux.35 fetches these by lock file.

PREREQUISITE (user has installed Docker; daemon may still need starting):
    sudo systemctl start docker      # password required; user runs this
    docker info                      # verify; alec is already in the docker group,
                                     # so docker itself needs no sudo

STEP 1 -- BUILD THE LINUX BINARY

    docker run --rm \
      --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
      -v /home/alec/code/dgen-audio:/src \
      -w /src \
      swift:6.3.3-jammy \
      swift build -c release --static-swift-stdlib \
        --product DGenLisp \
        --scratch-path /src/.build-container

  Image: swift:6.3.3-jammy. Jammy is Ubuntu 22.04 = glibc 2.35, the floor this
  bead targets, and 6.3.3 exactly matches the host toolchain so there is no
  version drift from what has already been validated locally. Do NOT substitute
  6.3-jammy or any -slim variant; slim omits build tooling.

  Each flag is load-bearing:
    --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"
        Without it the container runs as root and leaves ROOT-OWNED files in
        Alec's dgen-audio checkout, breaking later host builds and needing sudo
        to clean up.
    --scratch-path /src/.build-container
        /home/alec/code/dgen-audio/.build already holds host-toolchain artifacts
        for this same triple. Mixing toolchains in one scratch dir invites
        stale-artifact confusion. Add .build-container to dgen-audio's .gitignore.
    --static-swift-stdlib
        Needs /usr/lib/swift_static, which the image has and the host does NOT
        (host Swift is AUR swift-bin 6.3.3). This is exactly why a host build
        cannot produce this artifact. If SwiftPM rejects the flag, fall back to
        the driver options eseq-linux.15 proved work:
          -Xswiftc -static-stdlib -Xswiftc -Xclang-linker -Xswiftc -static-libgcc
        Confirm the image has it with:
          docker run --rm swift:6.3.3-jammy ls -d /usr/lib/swift_static

  Pin the upstream source at dgen-audio commit 68c6fba (branch linux-c-backend)
  or later.

STEP 2 -- VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING (non-negotiable; skipping this is how the
previous attempt shipped a broken binary)

  Result: /home/alec/code/dgen-audio/.build-container/release/DGenLisp
  Strip it, then:

    objdump -T <bin> | grep -oE 'GLIBC_[0-9.]+' | sort -Vu | tail -1
        MUST be <= 2.35. Anything higher means the build escaped the container.
        For reference the rejected host build reported GLIBC_2.44.

    ldd <bin>
        Expect ONLY libc, libm, libstdc++, libgcc_s, ld-linux.
        NO libswift*, libFoundation*, libdispatch, lib_FoundationICU.

  Then functionally smoke it -- compile a real patch and confirm it emits
  .c/.json/.so with processAbi dgen-host-abi-v1.

  Rename to DGenLisp-linux-x86_64.

STEP 3 -- THE MACOS ARTIFACT

  Cannot be produced in this container. Either build and publish it in a separate
  pass from Alec's Mac, or republish the existing 4.2 MB binary
  (sha256 f58b2abccd50234758365443644518a95632f2b2f0e6095b98fcd5c304b4ab63) as
  the macOS asset and note that its provenance predates this pipeline.
  State in the notes which was done. Do not leave this implicit.

STEP 4 -- PUBLISH

  github.com/universalsequences/dgen-audio has NO releases yet, so this bead also
  establishes the tag convention. Prefer a tool-qualified tag since the repo may
  later publish other products.

    gh release create dgenlisp-v0.1.0 \
      out/DGenLisp-linux-x86_64 \
      out/DGenLisp-macos-arm64 \
      --repo universalsequences/dgen-audio \
      --notes "upstream <sha>, glibc floor <x.yz>, static swift stdlib"

  Use RELEASE assets, never Actions build artifacts -- the latter expire (90 days
  default) and would silently break every clone and CI run once they lapse.
  Asset filenames must be target-qualified; do not publish a bare 'DGenLisp'.

  CHECK WHETHER dgen-audio IS PRIVATE. If it is, an unauthenticated curl from
  eseq-linux.35 will 404 and every fresh clone and CI run fails with a misleading
  error. Resolve here, not at CI time -- it decides whether the fetch needs a
  token or whether these belong somewhere public.

  Record per asset, since content/dgenlisp.lock pins exactly these: final URL,
  sha256, byte size, upstream commit, and for linux-x86_64 the measured glibc
  floor and the container image used.

SIZE, WORTH A LOOK WHILE HERE
  Linux is 62 MB against macOS at 4.1 MB for the same job; lib_FoundationICU is
  the likely bulk. If DGenLisp needs only FoundationEssentials rather than
  FoundationInternationalization, dropping that import upstream is a legitimate
  and probably large win. Less urgent now the artifact is out of git, but it
  still costs every CI run and fresh clone. Do it or explicitly defer it with
  reasoning.

PATH DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN
  The Swift Static Linux SDK (musl) would remove the glibc floor entirely rather
  than lowering it. Probed 2026-08-23: the 6.3.3 static SDK 404s at the documented
  URL and 'swift sdk list' reports none installed, while the ubuntu22.04 toolchain
  tarball for the same version returns 200. The container is the supported route
  today. Re-check on a future Swift release -- a static SDK would obsolete this
  entire recipe.
design: Container build on Alec's Linux box via Docker (installed, daemon currently disabled), image swift:6.3.3-jammy chosen because jammy is Ubuntu 22.04 / glibc 2.35 and 6.3.3 exactly matches the host toolchain so no version drift versus what has already been validated locally. Host build is impossible for this purpose: the AUR swift-bin package ships no /usr/lib/swift_static, and building on Arch glibc 2.44 is what produced the GLIBC_2.44 floor in the first place. The musl Static Linux SDK would be strictly better (no glibc floor at all) but has no 6.3.3 artifact bundle published, so it is deliberately deferred rather than attempted.
acceptance_criteria: Both artifacts are published from dgen-audio with stable versioned URLs and recorded sha256 digests; objdump -T on the published linux-x86_64 artifact reports a maximum GLIBC_ requirement at or below 2.35 and the base image is named in the notes; ldd shows no libswift*/libFoundation*/libdispatch/lib_FoundationICU entries; the artifact compiles a real patch emitting .c/.json/.so with processAbi dgen-host-abi-v1; NO binary is committed into the eseq repo by this bead; the ICU size investigation is either done or explicitly recorded as deferred with its reasoning

Downloaded published asset compiled toolchain/fixtures/scalar-synth.lisp and emitted nonempty .c/.json/.so; manifest processAbi was dgen-host-abi-v1 and inline ELF audit passed. macOS asset: https://github.com/universalsequences/dgen-audio/releases/download/dgenlisp-v0.1.0/DGenLisp-macos-arm64, sha256 f58b2abccd50234758365443644518a95632f2b2f0e6095b98fcd5c304b4ab63, 4235192 bytes; existing validated binary reused, with pre-pipeline provenance explicit in release notes. Repo confirmed PUBLIC. No binary or implementation file was added to eseq. dgen-audio commit 44bf840 contains only the required .gitignore entry and was pushed on linux-c-backend.

title: Add Linux CI workflow (build + full test suite on every push)
description:
The repo currently has no CI at all (no .github directory). The Linux port makes CI viable for the first time: GitHub's Linux runners are free/fast, while macOS runners are expensive — so Linux support is the prerequisite that unlocks putting the entire test suite behind every push.

This bead also protects the port itself: two platforms with no CI is worse than one, because the non-daily platform silently bitrots and cfg-gating mistakes accumulate. A Linux workflow converts the port from a one-time marketing artifact into a permanent repo-health asset.

Scope: add a GitHub Actions workflow that on push/PR (1) checks out, (2) installs the Rust toolchain + any Linux system deps the port needs (fonts, ALSA/audio headers, etc. — enumerate what the eseq-linux worktree actually required), (3) stages/derives the DGen toolchain or skips DGen-dependent tests with a documented reason, (4) runs cargo nextest run across the workspace with the 16 MiB RUST_MIN_STACK budget from .cargo/config.toml, (5) caches cargo registry + target dir to keep runtimes sane. Baseline for green as of 2026-08-20: full debug 4,272 passed / 32 skipped (see docs/test-suite-performance.md); on Linux, expect a different skip count from macOS-gated tests — record the Linux baseline in the workflow docs.
acceptance_criteria: Linux-verifiable only: workflow file exists and passes on a Linux runner (or via 'act'/manual run) at the tip of the eseq-linux branch; full nextest suite runs with zero failures; any skipped/excluded tests are enumerated with reasons in the workflow or docs; cargo caching is configured; no acceptance clause requires a macOS host.
notes: eseq-linux.35 landed (commit 9896fe57): CI must NOT build Swift or expect tracked DGenLisp binaries. Run ./scripts/fetch_dgenlisp.sh (idempotent, sha256-verified against content/dgenlisp.lock) before any step that compiles DGen patches; a missing compiler hard-fails naming that command. The dgen-toolchain stage (content/dgen-toolchain.lock) is still staged from a local dgen-audio checkout by rebuild_dgenlisp_tool.sh and remains CI-blocked until eseq-linux.30.

title: patcher_alignment_snaps_dragged_output_to_other_input_x fails on Linux
description:
Reproducible, isolated Linux failure found 2026-08-23 while auditing what is safe to work on before the macOS captures land.

  cargo test -p eseqlisp --features wgpu --lib -- --exact \
    widget_render::patcher::tests::patcher_alignment_snaps_dragged_output_to_other_input_x --test-threads=1

fails at crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/patcher/tests.rs:14403 with the panic payload '(0.0, 10.0)'.

This is NOT one of the two parallelism artifacts also seen in the same run (see the sibling bead for the /tmp collision, and eseq-tuw for the ACTIVE_THEME race) -- both of those pass when run alone. This one fails alone, deterministically.

It is also NOT the DGenLisp Mach-O problem (eseq-linux.14): there is no 'Exec format error' here, the assertion is a geometry comparison.

STRONG HYPOTHESIS worth checking first: the payload value 10.0 is exactly the Linux monospace cell_w measured by the eseq-linux.23 text-capture harness (metrics.json reports cell_w 10.0, cell_h 22.0 at font_size 16 / scale 1.0 with JetBrainsMonoNF-Regular). Patcher alignment snapping is grid-based, so this is very likely a real cell-metric dependency that happens to hold on macOS CoreText metrics and not on Linux fontdue metrics -- i.e. the first confirmed instance of the layout-shift risk the epic description warns about ('a different rasterizer shifts the entire interface... it will not fail loudly, it will look subtly wrong everywhere').

If that hypothesis holds, the fix is probably to make the test assert against measured cell metrics rather than a hardcoded constant, but confirm the production snapping code is metric-driven before changing the test -- if the SOURCE hardcodes a macOS cell width, the test is right and the code is wrong. Do not simply relax the assertion to make it green.

Related: eseq-linux.19 (condensed proportional face on Linux) is a different symptom of the same font-selection surface.
acceptance_criteria: The named test passes on Linux when run in isolation AND in a full-suite run; the fix is justified in the bead notes as either (a) test was over-specified to macOS metrics, or (b) production snapping code had a hardcoded metric -- with evidence for whichever; no assertion is weakened without that justification; the test still fails if snapping regresses
notes:
MERGED FROM eseq-linux.38 (duplicate, superseded 2026-08-24). Independent diagnosis from the .37 worker, which goes further than the original report:

align_dragged_primary_position returns the input position UNCHANGED instead of snapping x to 0.5; snap.snapped_x is presumably false. The test primes metrics via prime_patcher_text_metrics and node widths are explicitly set (12.0 / 20.0), BUT port x positions are derived from MEASURED TEXT -- which is the actual dependency.

Confirmed pre-existing at HEAD 6de7a320 in a detached worktree, so it is not a
regression from the DGenLisp harness work. After .37 landed this is the ONLY
remaining failure in the patcher suite: 488 passed / 1 failed in a clean shell
(independently re-verified 2026-08-24). That makes it the last thing standing
between Linux and a green patcher suite, hence the bump to P1.

The measured-text dependency is consistent with the original hypothesis here: the
panic payload 10.0 is exactly the Linux monospace cell_w from the eseq-linux.23
capture harness. Likely tracks the fontdue atlas swap and eseq-linux.18/.19 font
fallback producing different advance widths than the CoreText metrics the
expectation was authored against.

Decide explicitly: is the expectation font-dependent and should be made
metric-agnostic, or are Linux text metrics actually wrong? Do not weaken the
assertion without answering that.
close_reason: Made the alignment regression fixture derive port positions from production node geometry, independent of backend text metrics; isolated test and all 489 patcher tests pass on Linux.

comments.author: Alec Resende
comments.text: Diagnosis: the test fixture was over-specified to macOS text metrics; production snapping is already metric-driven. node_size_for_ports computes each rendered node width, and explicit PatchNode widths are minimums clamped against the auto-generated label width. The fixed b.x=12.77 therefore placed the relevant ports within the 0.6-cell snap threshold only under the original CoreText-derived width. On Linux, node_autogenerated_size_for_ports intentionally uses the terminal/wgpu backend's exact fixed-grid character count, making node a wider than 12 cells and leaving the ports outside the threshold. The regression test now derives both port offsets from node_size_for_ports/port_x_offset and positions the target to require a 0.5-cell output-to-input snap. It retains exact aligned-x and snapped_x assertions, so a snapping regression still fails. Validation: isolated test passed; full patcher module passed 489/489 with --features wgpu.

title: [macOS host] Capture and commit the three-way glyph golden set (CoreText@mac, fontdue@mac, fontdue@linux)
description:
REQUIRES A MACOS MACHINE. This is the only bead in the glyph-atlas chain that
does. Everything downstream becomes a Linux-runnable numeric/pixel diff once
this lands.

HANDOFF (agreed with user 2026-08-23): the worker pushes the `eseq-linux`
branch -- it currently has NO upstream configured -- and the user pulls it on
the Mac and runs the harness there. This bead is a RUN-AND-COMMIT bead, not a
design bead; eseq-linux.23 does the engineering so this session is short.

CAPTURE THREE POINTS, NOT TWO. The obvious comparison (CoreText vs Linux
fontdue) confounds two independent changes: the rasterizer changed AND the
platform/font-availability changed. Capture all three so they separate:

  1. coretext-macos    -- checkout 57b76e2a^ in a scratch worktree, apply the
                          eseq-linux.23 harness on top, run.
                          This is the ONLY way to get CoreText numbers: 57b76e2a

  2. fontdue-macos     -- checkout the branch HEAD, run the harness unmodified.
  3. fontdue-linux     -- already producible on the Linux host; the worker
                          generates this one, not you.

Point 2 is the one people skip and it is the most diagnostically useful: a
delta between 1 and 2 is purely the rasterizer swap, and a delta between 2 and
3 is purely the platform (font selection, DPI, scale). Reading only 1-vs-3
will send someone chasing the wrong cause. Note that eseq-linux.19 already
found load_system_ui_font picking a condensed face (NimbusSansNarrow) on
Linux -- that is exactly a 2-vs-3 class problem, and if it is still open when
this runs, expect it to show up in the deltas and say so in the notes rather
than treating it as rasterizer error.

crates/eseqlisp/tests/fixtures/ subdirectory eseq-linux.23 establishes.

and the exact commit each capture came from. Without those the goldens are
not reproducible and will rot silently.

DO NOT judge the deltas here -- just produce and commit the reference data.
Interpreting them and deciding whether they are acceptable is eseq-linux.20,
which is Linux-runnable once these files exist.

description:

check, split out so a Linux-only worker can build it without a Mac.

("feat(eseqlisp): replace CoreText glyph atlas") rewrote glyph_atlas.rs

At 57b76e2a^ the atlas is CoreText-backed with a different internal API than

unmodified at both commits. Instead:

  - keep the harness a standalone bin/example with a THIN adapter over
    whatever the atlas exposes at that commit
  - keep the adapter small enough that applying the harness onto 57b76e2a^
    is a cherry-pick plus a short shim, not a port

and confirm the harness builds and runs there on Linux. It will produce
garbage-or-error for the CoreText path on Linux (that is fine and expected --
CoreText cannot run here); what you are proving is that the harness COMPILES
and its non-CoreText plumbing works, so the Mac session is a run, not a
debugging session.

formatting, no timestamps, no absolute paths, no hostname):
  for each (font_size, scale_factor) in a FIXED list covering the real sizes
  and scales the UI uses:
    cell_w, cell_h, ascent, descent, leading

title: Judge the fontdue-vs-CoreText deltas against the committed goldens and sign off
description:
Carried over from eseq-linux.6, whose acceptance could not be run on the Linux
host that implemented 57b76e2a. RESTRUCTURED 2026-08-23: this bead no longer
requires a macOS machine. eseq-linux.23 builds the harness and eseq-linux.24
captures and commits the macOS reference data; this bead is now a pure diff
and judgement pass that runs on Linux.

The swap from CoreText to fontdb/fontdue changes layout-critical numbers and
appearance in ways that will not fail loudly:

  - cell_w: CTFont advances_for_glyphs('m') -> fontdue rasterize('m').advance_width
  - cell_h: CTFont ascent/descent/leading -> fontdue horizontal_line_metrics
    (hhea vs whatever CoreText reports)
  - SizedFontCache ascent/descent/leading for every proportional size
  - fontdue does no hinting and emits linear coverage; CoreText applies font
    smoothing and gamma, so glyphs will read thinner
  - copy_glyph_into_line rounds dst_y to whole rows, so vertical placement is
    integer-quantised where CoreText positioned subpixel

ATTRIBUTE EACH DELTA, DO NOT JUST MEASURE IT. The goldens are a three-way set
precisely so cause is separable:
    coretext-macos vs fontdue-macos  = the rasterizer swap, nothing else
    fontdue-macos   vs fontdue-linux = the platform, nothing else
A 1-vs-3 number alone conflates them and will send someone tuning the
rasterizer for what is actually a font-selection bug. eseq-linux.19
(load_system_ui_font picks condensed NimbusSansNarrow on Linux) is a known
2-vs-3 contributor -- if it is still open, expect it in the deltas and label
it as such rather than charging it to fontdue.

Note one pre-existing inconsistency the rewrite already FIXED, so do not read
it as a regression: old SizedFontCache::new seeded line_metrics under key
(base_font_size*10) using a font built at base_font_size WITHOUT the scale
multiplier, while sized_font() for the same key would have used size*scale.
The new cache has no seed and is self-consistent.

"Bounded" is not defined anywhere yet -- part of this bead is choosing the
threshold and writing down why. A sub-pixel cell_w drift is cosmetic; a
whole-pixel cell_h drift reflows the entire UI grid, because the grid lays
out on these numbers (WidgetViewport.cell_w/cell_h, metal_backend.rs:7629
text_cell_w/h, :7721, :7974). Treat those two cases differently.
acceptance_criteria: Runs on Linux against the committed goldens from eseq-linux.24 -- no macOS host required. cell_w/cell_h/ascent/descent/leading deltas computed for all three points (coretext-macos, fontdue-macos, fontdue-linux) at every captured font size and scale; each delta attributed to rasterizer swap (1-vs-2) or platform (2-vs-3); a bounded threshold is chosen and written down with its rationale; PNG diffs reviewed and any visible regression either fixed or filed as a new bead; sign-off recorded in the bead notes

title: Glyph atlas has no font fallback: a missing exact font name kills all text rendering
description:
Regression introduced by 57b76e2a (eseq-linux.6). glyph_atlas::load_named_font() resolves by exact PostScript name, then by exact family name, and returns None if neither hits. GlyphAtlas::new() propagates that None, so MetalBackend::self.atlas / self.text_atlas become None.

Downstream that is fatal, not cosmetic: metal_backend.rs:3913, :5006, :5363, :5943, :5994 do self.atlas.as_mut().ok_or(BackendError::MetalError)?, and :3860 / :4817 bail out of the frame entirely. mono cell_w/cell_h also come from the atlas (:3752-3784), so layout collapses too.

The old CoreText path could not fail this way: CTFont::with_name() always returns a font, silently substituting the system font, and the code only logged a warning.

Reproduced on this Linux box (JetBrains Mono Nerd Font installed at /usr/share/fonts/TTF):
  GlyphAtlas::new("JetBrainsMono-Regular", 13.0) -> None
  GlyphAtlas::new("JetBrains Mono Nerd Font", 13.0) -> Some (PS name JetBrainsMonoNF-Regular)
The hardcoded name at metal_backend.rs:3774 and :6119/:6129 is "JetBrainsMono-Regular", so any machine carrying the Nerd Font variant (or no JetBrains Mono at all) gets a dead UI.
acceptance_criteria: load_named_font falls back through a monospace preference list and finally Family::Monospace so it can only fail when the machine has no font at all; a test asserts GlyphAtlas::new with a deliberately bogus font name still returns Some
close_reason: Fallback chain verified: exact name -> normalized family stem -> monospace preference list -> Family::Monospace -> any monospaced face -> any face. Reviewer added the stem match and the two last-resort steps (cb7a9a24 alone could still return None on a box without a fontconfig monospace alias, and picked Liberation Mono over the reporting machine's own JetBrainsMono Nerd Font). 7 glyph_atlas tests pass; the 41 other eseqlisp lib failures reproduce identically at clean HEAD (dgen toolchain exec-format + /tmp collisions).

=== URGENT ADDENDUM 2026-08-23: -static-stdlib IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT ===
Measured on the Arch box after this bead was started. Read before building.

1. GLIBC FLOOR IS THE REAL PORTABILITY BLOCKER, AND STATIC-STDLIB DOES NOT FIX IT.
   Static-linking the Swift stdlib removes the libswift*/libFoundation*/libdispatch
   dependencies. It leaves glibc DYNAMIC. objdump -T on the current build shows this
   binary already demands very new versioned glibc symbols:
       atan2f  GLIBC_2.43
       log10f  GLIBC_2.43
       sqrtf   GLIBC_2.43
       fmodf   GLIBC_2.38
       __isoc23_strtoull GLIBC_2.38
   This host is glibc 2.44 (Arch). A binary with a GLIBC_2.43 floor will fail to load
   on essentially every other Linux in use -- Ubuntu 24.04 is 2.39, Debian 12 is 2.36,
   typical CI images are older still. It would run on Alec's Surface and nowhere else,
   which is the exact failure mode this bead exists to prevent -- just with a different
   cause than the Swift runtime.

   CONSEQUENCE: building the vendored binary ON THIS ARCH HOST IS WRONG. It must be
   built against an old glibc -- a container based on e.g. Ubuntu 22.04 (2.35) or
   similar -- so the floor lands somewhere broadly usable. Pick the floor deliberately,
   state it in the notes, and verify it after building with:
       objdump -T <binary> | grep -oE 'GLIBC_[0-9.]+' | sort -Vu | tail -1

2. THE STATIC STDLIB MAY NOT BE INSTALLED HERE.
   Swift is 6.3.3 (swift-6.3.3-RELEASE, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) but there is NO
   /usr/lib/swift_static/linux/ directory. --static-swift-stdlib / -static-stdlib
   needs that to exist. Expect the build to fail until a toolchain that ships
   swift_static is used -- which the old-glibc container from point 1 should provide
   anyway, so solve both together rather than separately.

3. USE THE SWIFTPM FLAG, NOT THE RAW SWIFTC ONE.
   Prefer: swift build -c release --static-swift-stdlib
   over:   swift build -c release -Xswiftc -static-stdlib
   The SwiftPM flag is the supported spelling and handles linking the whole product
   correctly. (This supersedes the command named in the description.)

4. ICU IS AN EXTRA WEIGHT AND AN EXTRA RISK.
   The binary pulls lib_FoundationICU.so (FoundationInternationalization). Static
   linking that pulls ICU data in and will inflate the artifact well beyond the
   11.7 MB stripped-dynamic figure. Measure it. If the result is unreasonably large,
   check whether the tool actually needs FoundationInternationalization or only
   FoundationEssentials -- dropping the internationalization import upstream would be
   a legitimate size fix, and is a smaller change than it sounds.

5. RESIDUAL NON-SWIFT DEPS after static-stdlib should be only:
       libc.so.6  libm.so.6  libstdc++.so.6  libgcc_s.so.1  ld-linux-x86-64.so.2

statically linked, OR the glibc floor cannot be brought below roughly 2.35. Either
one alone makes the committed-binary decision unworkable and sends this back to the
staging option the user considered and rejected.

title: Cross-platform glyph atlas: replace CoreText (layout-critical, top risk)
description:
TOP RISK OF THE WHOLE PORT. crates/eseqlisp/src/ui/glyph_atlas.rs is 554
lines of CoreText with no non-macOS path at all (cfg gates at :9 and :553).

What it does: CTFont::with_name, CGBitmapContextCreate, rasterizes glyphs
into a shared R8Unorm atlas packed with etagere, plus SizedFontCache (:242)
for line metrics and a separate ProportionalGlyphAtlas.

Why it is the risk: it is load-bearing for LAYOUT, not just drawing.
  :84  cell_w derived from font.advances_for_glyphs()
  :81  cell_h = ceil(ascent + descent + leading)
and the entire UI grid lays out on those - see WidgetViewport.cell_w/cell_h
and ui/metal_backend.rs:7629 (text_cell_w/h), :7721, :7974. Swap the
rasterizer and the whole interface shifts. This will NOT fail loudly; it
will look subtly wrong everywhere (metrics, hinting, gamma).

Options, roughly in order of completeness vs weight:
  - cosmic-text: shaping + font fallback + layout. Heaviest, most complete.
  - swash (raster) + fontdue/ab_glyph: lighter, you own layout.
Whatever is chosen must also serve the ProportionalText primitive, not just
the monospace grid.

Also note the CoreText Y-up convention baked into the atlas (:6, :33, :186)
- v is stored Y-up and flipped in the shader. Pick a convention and make it
explicit rather than inheriting CoreText's by accident.

Suggested approach: build a metrics comparison harness first. Render the
same buffer through CoreText and the candidate rasterizer, diff cell_w/cell_h
/ascent/descent and a few full screenshots, BEFORE committing to a library.
acceptance_criteria: Glyph and proportional atlases build on Linux; metrics harness shows cell_w/cell_h/ascent/descent deltas vs CoreText are understood and bounded; screenshots of the same buffer compared side by side
notes:
Reviewed 2026-08-23 against commit 57b76e2a.

Verified on this Linux host:
- cargo test -p eseqlisp --lib glyph_atlas: 2 passed (cpu_atlases_measure_and_rasterize_on_every_platform, atlas_uvs_follow_top_down_bitmap_rows)
- cargo check -p eseqlisp --features wgpu --all-targets: clean
- cargo check -p eseqlisp --target x86_64-apple-darwin --all-targets: clean (only a pre-existing unused-import warning in editor/widget_focus.rs:1170)
- no CoreText/CTFont/CGBitmapContext references remain in crates/

Correctness confirmed by reading: the Y convention is right. The old doc comment claiming a v = 1.0 - v shader flip was stale - neither the old MSL (text frag sampled in.uv directly) nor the old vertex emission flipped anything. CGBitmapContext memory rows are top-down, so drawing at CG y=descent already put the baseline at memory row cell_h-descent. The new code reproduces exactly that with baseline = cell_h - descent and top-down fontdue output, and the vertex emission at metal_backend.rs:7383-7400 is byte-identical to before. Proportional offset_x replacing the hardcoded -2.0*scale padding is a genuine fix for overhanging glyphs.

  :1192 compile_sdf_to_metal_with_state
  :1285 compile_sdf_expr
  :1289 compile_sdf_expr_with_theme
  :1069 SdfShaderOutput
  :1074 metal_safe_symbol
  :1078 uniform_layout
  :1090 emit_uniform_declarations
  :1023 expr_returns_float4

Most of the emitter is expression-level and type names appear in ~61 places
(float2/float3/float4). Consider extracting a small Emitter trait over type
names + statement forms rather than forking the file.

Real divergences to handle, not just renames:
- Types: float4 -> vec4<f32>, float2 -> vec2<f32>, float3 -> vec3<f32>
- Statements: `float4 x = expr;` -> `let x = expr;` / `var x = expr;`
  (the emitter pushes raw C-style decls, e.g. :263, :271, :337, :341, :348)
- WGSL has NO implicit numeric conversions. MSL happily mixes int/float
  literals; WGSL will reject. Audit format_float (:1008) and every literal
  site.
- Uniform declarations and binding model differ substantially
  (emit_uniform_declarations, uniform_layout).
- Function/entry-point syntax and attribute syntax.

Test strategy: golden tests that run BOTH emitters over the full content/
shader corpus (content/ui/materials.lisp, sequencer.lisp, step-grid.lisp,
legacy/mixer.lisp, browser.lisp, transport.lisp, sound-palette.lisp,
effects/*.lisp - 17 lisp files reference shaders). Assert the WGSL compiles
via naga. Snapshot both outputs so MSL cannot regress.
acceptance_criteria: Every shader in the content/ corpus emits WGSL that naga accepts; MSL output byte-identical to before (snapshot); golden tests cover both emitters

title: Linux port: wgpu graphics target, cross-platform text, portable dgen host
description:
Port eseq to Linux. Three dependency clusters: graphics (Metal -> wgpu),
text (CoreText -> cross-platform rasterizer), and dgen/audio host
(Accelerate + Mach-O + CoreAudio assumptions).

KEY ARCHITECTURAL FINDING (scoping pass 2026-08-22):
`MetalPrimitive` is not Metal. widget_render/mod.rs:754 defines it, and it
plus WidgetInstance (:538), WidgetViewport (:558), MetalRectPrimitive
(:585), MetalProportionalTextPrimitive (:619) and ndc_bounds (:4283) are
plain #[repr(C)] data - f32 arrays, Rect, Color, String. Zero objc. They
are only cfg(target_os="macos")-gated and misleadingly named. eseq already
has a backend-neutral retained-mode display list.

Evidence: `cargo check -p eseqlisp --lib` on Linux yields 31 errors and
EVERY one is "cannot find MetalPrimitive/WidgetInstance/WidgetViewport/
ndc_bounds in super" - the cfg gate, not a real platform dependency.
Ungating them makes ~100k LOC of widget_render/ compile on Linux.

Corollary: ui/metal_backend.rs is 10,954 lines but only ~280 touch
MTL*/objc2/Retained. The other 97% is instance-buffer and geometry
building that is already API-agnostic.

Shader work splits in two:
- GENERATED (free): content/*.lisp authors SDF shaders in eseqlisp
  (defwidget :shader, material, lighting - see content/ui/materials.lisp).
  lang/sdf_codegen.rs (1858 LOC) compiles them to MSL via a MetalEmitter
  struct (:24). User content needs zero porting; add a WgslEmitter beside it.
- HAND-WRITTEN (the grind): ~3,300 lines of MSL in Rust string literals.
  1,149 in ui/metal_backend.rs (8 pipelines) and ~2,165 across 25 widgets'
  metal_fragment_shader() trait methods.

TOP RISK: text. ui/glyph_atlas.rs is 554 lines of CoreText with no non-mac
path, and it is load-bearing for LAYOUT not just drawing - cell_w comes from
font.advances_for_glyphs(), cell_h from ascent+descent+leading, and the whole
UI grid is laid out on those. A different rasterizer shifts the entire
interface. It will not fail loudly, it will look subtly wrong everywhere.

FREE WINS: no MIDI anywhere (no CoreMIDI, no midir). No NSOpenPanel/
NSSavePanel. AppKit surface in metal_backend.rs is only NSView (CAMetalLayer
attach), NSColor, NSAppearance (dark mode), NSHapticFeedback. winit 0.29 is
already a dependency, just sitting inside the macOS-only dep block.

STRATEGY: add wgpu as a genuine third target beside TUI and Metal. Do not
collapse Metal into wgpu - that would regress a tuned renderer. Revisit later.

SCOPE DECISION -- TRAINING IS OUT OF SCOPE FOR LINUX (user, 2026-08-23).
DO NOT RE-LITIGATE. Do not file beads to port it. Do not "fix" it as a bug.

DGenLisp's `train` subcommand (gradient/CMA-ES parameter fitting against a
target sample) is Metal-based upstream and has no Linux implementation. The
Linux port in dgen-audio (branch linux-c-backend, 68c6fba) deliberately
covers `compile` only. `compile` is the load-bearing path -- it is what the
patcher, instruments and effects use, and it works on Linux, verified.

The affected surface in this repo is small and bounded:
  crates/sequencer/src/learn_job.rs        builds the `train` argv
                                           (:590 "train", :595 --seed-params,
                                           :597 --job-dir, :615 --epochs,
                                           :632 --search cma-es)
  content/ui/patch-learn.lisp              the Learn UI, incl. cma-es stages
  crates/sequencer/ui/capture-fixtures/patch-learn-optimizer-progress.lisp
  crates/sequencer/src/ui/state_values/tests.rs:16189

What "out of scope" MUST mean in practice: the feature is unavailable on Linux
and says so. It must not mean an unhandled failure when a user opens Learn.
That degradation work is tracked separately and IS in scope -- see the
"training unavailable on Linux" bead. Everything beyond that -- porting the
optimizer, a CPU trainer, a wgpu trainer -- is out.

Revisit only if the upstream dgen repo grows a non-Metal trainer.
VENDORING DECISION -- SUPERSEDED, THEN SETTLED (user, 2026-08-23).
Recorded so the reversal is not re-litigated in either direction.

FIRST decision: track both binaries at per-target paths. Implemented in
eseq-linux.15 / ed326340.

REVERSED the same day once the numbers were measured:
  Linux binary  64 MB on disk, 62 MB compressed in git (binaries barely compress)
  macOS binary  4.1 MB
  .git total    191 MB -- so one blob was already a third of all history
  cadence       DGenLisp is expected to change WEEKLY OR MORE
  => roughly 3 GB of permanent history per year. Untenable at any binary size.

SETTLED shape: publish per-target artifacts from dgen-audio; eseq commits only
content/dgenlisp.lock (url + sha256 + upstream commit + glibc floor) and fetches
into a gitignored path. Repo growth per update is zero, and a contributor still
needs neither a Swift toolchain nor the dgen-audio checkout -- which was the
property that motivated the original tracked-binary choice.

Rejected alternatives and why:
  stage from a sibling checkout  -- the existing dgen-toolchain pattern, but it
      requires every contributor and CI to have dgen-audio plus Swift, losing
      the zero-setup property.
  keep tracking, shrink first    -- even at a hoped-for 15 MB, weekly updates
      are ~780 MB/year and need periodic history rewrites.
  git LFS                        -- keeps clones small but adds LFS setup for
      every contributor and CI, plus quota, plus a migration rewrite.

Chain: .33 (build old-glibc + publish, upstream) -> .35 (lock + fetch, eseq)
       -> .34 (excise the blob from unpushed history) -> unblocks pushing the
       branch, which .24 needs for the macOS handoff.

STILL TRUE from the first decision, do not undo: the Swift runtime MUST be
statically linked (eseq-linux.15 solved this), and there are two targets, not
one -- static linking never collapses macOS and Linux into a single binary.

title: CLAUDE.md cheap clean-HEAD recipe is unsound: dead toolchain export + shared target dir runs the wrong binary
description:
Two defects in the "Cheap clean-HEAD check" recipe in CLAUDE.md (also mirrored in AGENTS.md).

1. It exports
     ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT="$root/crates/sequencer/tools/dgen-toolchain"
   which does not exist in any Linux checkout (gitignored ~147 MB stage, never
   produced for Linux -- see eseq-linux.30). app_paths warns and ignores a
   non-directory override, so it is inert-but-misleading; the patcher harness no
   longer reads it at all after eseq-linux.37. Either drop the export or make the
   recipe set it only when the stage exists.

2. Sharing CARGO_TARGET_DIR between the disposable worktree and the working
   checkout SILENTLY POISONS the working checkout. Observed 2026-08-24:

     - ran the recipe against /tmp/eseq-head-test with
       CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/alec/code/eseq/target
     - afterwards, two consecutive `cargo test -p eseqlisp --lib` runs from
       /home/alec/code/eseq executed the HEAD-built test binary, not the working
       tree: panics reported source lines exactly 226 lower, matching the line
       delta of the uncommitted edit. Tests that pass in the working tree reported
       as failing.
     - `touch` on the edited source forced a rebuild and the failures vanished.

   Cargo reuses the same unit fingerprint for the two checkouts, so whichever ran
   last wins. Anyone using this recipe to "check whether a failure is pre-existing"
   can get the exact opposite answer. The recipe should either use a separate
   target dir for the worktree, or say explicitly that the working checkout must be
   rebuilt (touch a source file / cargo build) after each worktree run.
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md no longer instruct exporting a path that does not exist, and the clean-HEAD recipe cannot silently make the working checkout run the worktree binary.

description:
Implements the epic's scope decision (user, 2026-08-23) that the DGenLisp "train" subcommand is out of scope for Linux because it is Metal-based upstream. "Out of scope" must mean "unavailable and clearly labelled", NOT "crashes or hangs when a user clicks Learn". title: Hermetic dgen toolchain is arm64-only; Linux compiles fall back to the system compiler
description:
Found 2026-08-23 while validating the Linux DGenLisp binary.

content/dgen-toolchain.lock pins a single archive with no platform or arch dimension:
  archive       dgen-toolchain-20.1.8-arm64.tar.gz
  llvm_version  20.1.8
  dgen_abi_version 1

The staged stage directory crates/sequencer/tools/dgen-toolchain/ is gitignored (~147 MB) and is EMPTY on this Linux box -- nothing has ever staged an x86_64 equivalent, and the pinned archive is arm64 anyway.

Despite that, compiling through the Linux DGenLisp succeeded and emitted a working .so. That means the Linux path silently fell back to the SYSTEM compiler rather than the hermetic clang/lld stage. Reproduced with:

  DGenLisp compile t.lisp -o out --name patcher_dgen_compile_test \
    --sample-rate 44100 --voices 12
  -> out/patcher_dgen_compile_test.{c,json,so}, processAbi dgen-host-abi-v1

WHY THIS MATTERS: hermeticity is the whole point of the staged toolchain -- pinned LLVM version, reproducible codegen, no dependence on whatever clang a contributor happens to have. On Linux that guarantee is currently absent and, worse, absent SILENTLY: the build succeeds, so nobody notices that two machines can produce different audio binaries from identical source.

SCOPE:
 • Give content/dgen-toolchain.lock a platform/arch dimension (archive + sha256 per target) rather than one flat entry.
 • Establish where an x86_64-linux toolchain archive comes from -- built upstream in dgen-audio, or fetched. Coordinate with eseq-linux.15, which touches rebuild_dgenlisp_tool.sh (the script that stages the archive and maintains this lock).
 • Decide the fallback policy explicitly and implement it: either hard-fail when no matching stage exists for the host target, or warn loudly. Silent fallback is the actual bug here.
 • DGenLisp already accepts --toolchain-root and honours DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_STAGE_ROOT; eseq passes ESEQ_DGEN_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT. Verify the whole chain reports, rather than swallows, a missing or wrong-arch stage.

This is independent of whether the DGenLisp binary itself is committed -- it is about the compiler the binary invokes.
acceptance_criteria: content/dgen-toolchain.lock carries per-target archive identities; a missing or wrong-arch toolchain stage produces a clear diagnostic instead of a silent system-compiler fallback, with a test covering that path; the source of an x86_64-linux toolchain archive is documented in the bead notes even if staging it is deferred; compiling a patch on Linux either uses the hermetic stage or fails loudly saying it cannot

THE ORDERING IS THE WHOLE POINT: you cannot capture a wgpu-vs-Metal
comparison before the wgpu side renders. So .7 and .8 now own "renders
correctly on Linux, captures produced", and this bead owns "compare against
macOS and sign off". Blocked on both.

     it must be pushed first).
  2. Run the whole-frame capture path on the Metal backend for the same fixed

title: load_system_ui_font picks a condensed face on Linux (NimbusSansNarrow)
description:
glyph_atlas::load_system_ui_font() has a macOS preference list (SFPro-Regular, .AppleSystemUIFont, Helvetica) and nothing for Linux - it falls straight through to Query{families: [Family::SansSerif]}.

Probed on this box: SizedFontCache::new(1.0) resolves to NimbusSansNarrow-Regular. That is a *condensed* face, so every proportional advance is materially narrower than a normal sans.

Needs a Linux preference list (DejaVu Sans / Noto Sans / Liberation Sans / Cantarell / Inter) before the generic SansSerif fallback.

title: aubio-sys fails to build on Linux (strncasecmp implicit declaration under -std=c99)
description:
`cargo check -p sequencer` fails on Linux: aubio-sys 0.2.1 compiles its vendored aubio C sources with `-std=c99`, which hides POSIX declarations under glibc. `aubio/src/utils/strutils.c:39` then errors with 'implicit declaration of function strncasecmp' (an error, not a warning, under modern GCC/C23 defaults).

Reproduced during review of eseq-linux.4 on Arch (gcc, glibc). macOS is unaffected because Apple libc exposes strncasecmp regardless of the std level.

This blocks building the sequencer crate at all on Linux, so no workspace-wide build or test run is possible there yet.

Options: set CFLAGS/-D_GNU_SOURCE or -std=gnu99 via a build override, patch/vendor aubio-sys, or move to a maintained fork.
acceptance_criteria: aubio-sys compiles on Linux: 'cargo build -p aubio-sys' (or the equivalent isolated build) succeeds with no implicit-declaration error from strutils.c. NOTE: this bead alone does NOT make 'cargo check -p sequencer' pass -- crates/sequencer/audiograph/dgen_host_services.c:14 independently fails on a missing Accelerate/Accelerate.h, which is eseq-linux.9. Verify by confirming the aubio-sys build-script failure is gone and that the NEXT build-script failure reported is the Accelerate one, not an aubio one. Whole-crate 'cargo check -p sequencer' green is the acceptance of eseq-linux.9, which lands second.
notes: Vendored aubio-sys 0.2.1 and patched its header detection to include POSIX <strings.h> when available. Validation: cargo build -p aubio-sys passes on Linux; cargo check -p sequencer proceeds to the expected Accelerate/Accelerate.h failure tracked by eseq-linux.9.
close_reason: Patched vendored aubio-sys to detect/include strings.h; isolated aubio-sys build passes on Linux.

title: SDF lighting cost: 5x field evaluation per pixel from finite-difference normals
description:
The generated SDF lighting path is the most likely first perf wall on
non-Apple GPUs, and it is fixable entirely in the emitter - no content
changes.

crates/eseqlisp/src/lang/sdf_codegen.rs:640-710 computes the surface normal
by FINITE DIFFERENCES: it evaluates the SDF field at four offset positions
(left, right, up, down) to derive dx/dy, then builds
normalize(float3(dx, dy, 1.0)). So every lit widget evaluates its ENTIRE SDF
expression 5 times per pixel. On top of that, per pixel:
  - 2x normalize (normal, light vector)
  - 2x dot (diffuse, specular)
  - 1x pow() for Blinn-Phong specular (:701-707)

This is not a rare path. content/ui/materials.lisp puts :lighting on
slider-material and slider-material2, so every slider and knob in the UI
pays it.

On Apple silicon this never surfaced (GPU sits ~10%). On an Intel UHD 620 -
roughly 6-8x less ALU, immediate-mode blending instead of TBDR, and DDR4
bandwidth shared with the CPU and the audio engine - this is the term most
likely to dominate.

Options, cheapest first:
  1. Cache the base SDF evaluation and reuse it across the 4 offset taps
     where the expression allows - may cut 5 evaluations toward 4.
  2. Analytic normals for the primitive shapes that have them
     (rounded-rect, circle), falling back to finite differences only for
     arbitrary composed fields.
  3. Replace pow() with a cheaper specular approximation.
  4. A quality tier: emit flat shading (drop :lighting to its :color term)
     under a runtime/backend flag. Lets the Linux target ship before the
     optimization work lands, and gives low-end hardware an escape hatch.

Measure before choosing. Build a shader-cost probe on a representative
sequencer buffer (many sliders and knobs visible) and compare frame time
with lighting on vs forced flat, on BOTH macOS and the UHD 620 box, before
committing to an approach.

Do this work in the emitter so it benefits the Metal target too.

title: Audio on Linux: verify cpal/ALSA block size, add SCHED_FIFO RT worker priority
description:
Audio is close to free but has two real gaps.

cpal (probably fine): usage is vanilla - crates/sequencer/src/audio/stream.rs
:145 cpal::default_host(), :150 StreamConfig with
:153 BufferSize::Fixed(block_size), f32 output. Dev box confirms ALSA 1.2.16
headers present and PipeWire's pulse server running.

    CoreAudio. Confirm the requested block size actually lands, and that the
    audiograph's fixed-block assumptions hold if it does not.
  - Consider enabling cpal's `jack` feature for low latency.
  - Check device enumeration in stream.rs:176-190 (supports_f32 probing)

already guards Mach with `#if __has_include(<mach/mach.h>)` (:21), and
crates/sequencer/src/audio/engine.rs:392 sets
`mach_rt_default = cfg!(target_os = "macos") && workers > 0`. So it degrades
SAFELY on Linux - but "degrades" means the audio graph worker threads run at
normal priority and will glitch under load.
  - Add a Linux path: pthread_setschedparam with SCHED_FIFO, mirroring what
    thread_policy_set THREAD_TIME_CONSTRAINT_POLICY does at
    graph_engine.c:579.

    permission-denied case gracefully and log it, matching the existing

    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) equivalent.

title: dgen dylib pipeline: ELF audit, -shared/-fPIC flags, .dylib -> .so
description:
The dgen compile-and-load pipeline assumes Mach-O, arm64, and .dylib.

1) crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/dgen/dgen_audit.rs validates every
generated dylib before load:
  :18  use object::read::macho::{LoadCommandVariant, MachHeader}
  :91  MachHeader64::<Endianness>::parse
  :109 checks cputype == CPU_TYPE_ARM64
  :119 checks filetype == MH_DYLIB
  :243 MachOFile64 symbol walk
  :37  hardcodes "/usr/bin/clang"
  :364 test fixtures shell out to /usr/bin/cc with -dynamiclib, -arch arm64,
       -install_name @rpath/{name}.dylib
Needs an ELF sibling. crates/sequencer/Cargo.toml currently enables only the
`macho` feature on the `object` crate - add `elf`. Decide what the Linux
audit actually asserts (ET_DYN, EM_X86_64/EM_AARCH64, DT_NEEDED limited to
libc/libm, no unexpected undefined symbols).

2) Compile flags and naming across lisp_host/dgen/:
  -dynamiclib     -> -shared
  -install_name   -> -soname (or omit)
  -arch arm64     -> drop or map to the host arch
  add -fPIC
  .dylib          -> .so throughout the cache paths
See instrument_compile.rs:373 (dylib_name format), effect_compile.rs:470
(the compile Command), and the dylib_cache module
(lisp_host/dgen/dylib_cache, re-exported at lisp_host/mod.rs:58).

3) There are ~30 dylib_cache.acquire() call sites in app/edit.rs,
app/effects.rs, app/fx_chain.rs - they should not need changes if the naming
is centralized, but verify.

dlopen/dlclose semantics themselves are fine on Linux. Watch for
RTLD_LOCAL/RTLD_GLOBAL differences on hot-swap and for symbol interposition
behaving differently than on macOS two-level namespaces.

Related: the eseq-toolchain epic.
acceptance_criteria: A lisp DSP source compiles to a .so, passes an ELF audit, dlopens, and produces audio on Linux; hot-swap works across reloads; macOS path unchanged
notes:
SCOPE REDUCED 2026-08-23 by the upstream Linux port (dgen-audio linux-c-backend @ 68c6fba).

Item 2 of the description -- the compile flags and .dylib -> .so rename -- is largely handled INSIDE DGenLisp upstream, not in eseq. Verified by running the Linux binary directly:
  DGenLisp compile t.lisp -o out --name X --sample-rate 44100 --voices 12
  -> out/X.c, out/X.json, out/X.SO  (already ELF, already .so, no eseq change involved)
So do not start by rewriting -dynamiclib/-install_name/-arch flags; first check which of those paths eseq still drives itself versus which DGenLisp now owns. The manifest still reports processAbi 'dgen-host-abi-v1', so the ABI constraint in eseq-linux.9 is intact.

title: dgen host services: drop Accelerate/vDSP (4 symbols) for a portable FFT
description:
crates/sequencer/build.rs unconditionally emits
`cargo:rustc-link-lib=framework=Accelerate`, and
crates/sequencer/audiograph/dgen_host_services.c:14 does
`#include <Accelerate/Accelerate.h>`. Neither exists on Linux.

Good news: the vDSP surface is narrow. Only 4 symbols across 11 call sites:
  vDSP_create_fftsetup
  vDSP_fft_zip
  vDSP_zvma
  vDSP_Length

The DGen ABI v1 host-services table is vDSP-backed; generated DGen dylibs
themselves stay libSystem-only and never link Accelerate, so this is
confined to the host.

Scope:
- Replace the FFT with a portable implementation (kissfft or pffft vendored
  into audiograph/, or expose rustfft through the host-services table -
  rustfft 6.2 is already a sequencer dependency).
- Replace vDSP_zvma (complex vector multiply-add) - trivial to hand-write.
- Make the Accelerate link in build.rs conditional on target_os = macos.
- Keep the ABI v1 host-services table layout byte-identical so existing
  generated dylibs stay valid.

Also confirm the split-radix / packed-complex convention vDSP_fft_zip uses
matches whatever replaces it - this is the classic place to silently get
scaling or bin ordering wrong. Add a numeric test comparing outputs before
switching macOS over.

Related: the eseq-toolchain epic covers shipping the embedded dgen toolchain.
acceptance_criteria: audiograph builds and links on Linux with no Accelerate; 'cargo check -p sequencer' succeeds on Linux (this is the bead that finally turns the sequencer crate green there -- verified 2026-08-23 that Accelerate is the second of exactly two build-script blockers, the first being eseq-linux.16); numeric test shows the replacement FFT matches vDSP output within tolerance; ABI v1 host-services table layout unchanged

title: Port 25 widget fragment shaders to WGSL (~2165 lines)
description:
Port the per-widget fragment shaders to WGSL. ~2,165 lines of MSL across 25
widget modules in crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/. Depends on
eseq-linux.2 (backend-tagged trait) and the WIDGET_SHADER_PREAMBLE port in
eseq-linux.7, since each of these is concatenated onto that preamble.

By MSL volume:
  sound_glyph 364, mod 247, button 224, response_curve_editor 158,
  adsr_editor 158, matrix 128, phaser_notch 126, modulator_curve 87,
  knob_number 84, roar_shaper 80, multiband_meter 64, roar_filter 63,
  vslider 51, tree 49, plus box_widget knob number_picker scroll timeline
  hslider toggle text_input dropdown.

Note the overlap with eseq-linux.3: some of these hand-written shaders do
work the SDF DSL can already express. Where that is true, consider deleting
the hand-written MSL and moving the widget to a defwidget :shader instead of
maintaining two translations. Evaluate per widget; do not force it.

and half-precision assumptions, texture sampling. Expect a subset to compile

widget in isolation, macOS vs Linux, pixel diff) before porting in bulk.
crates/eseqlisp/src/bin/eseqlisp_capture.rs may already be a starting point.

The per-widget pixel diff vs macOS is NOT part of this bead -- it is eseq-linux.25.

title: Port the 8 core MSL pipelines in metal_backend.rs to WGSL (~1150 lines)
description:
Port the 8 hand-written MSL pipelines in crates/eseqlisp/src/ui/metal_backend.rs
to WGSL. ~1,149 lines of MSL. Mechanical but real.

  :100  SHADER_SRC                    text quad (vert + frag)
  :147  PROP_FRAG_SRC                 proportional text fragment
  :171  IMAGE_SHADER_SRC              image_vert / image_frag
  :247  PATCH_CABLE_SHADER_SRC        patch_cable_vert (:292) / frag (:467)
  :513  WIDGET_SHADER_PREAMBLE        instance struct, varyings, SDF utils
  :572  DEFAULT_WIDGET_VERTEX_SHADER  widget_vert
  :762  WAVETABLE_SHADER_SRC          wavetable_vert / wavetable_frag
  :924  WAVEFORM_SHADER_SRC           waveform_vert / waveform_frag
  :1170 LIVE_SPECTROGRAM_SHADER_SRC   live_spectrogram_vert / frag

Plus crates/eseqlisp/shaders/button_surface.metal (96 lines), the only
standalone .metal file.

The WIDGET_SHADER_PREAMBLE is the important one - it defines the shared
WidgetInstance struct, WidgetVaryings, and the SDF utility functions that
every per-widget fragment shader (eseq-linux.8) is concatenated onto. Port
it first and get it right.

Known translation hazards beyond type renames:
- WGSL has no implicit numeric conversions; MSL mixes int/float freely.
- [[stage_in]] / [[buffer(n)]] / [[vertex_id]] / [[instance_id]] ->
  @location / @group+@binding / @builtin.
- Texture sampling model differs substantially (separate sampler objects).
- MSL fast-math and half precision defaults may be silently relied on.
  Expect "compiles fine, renders differently" on a subset.

Suggested order: text quad first (proves the glyph atlas end to end), then
image, then widget preamble + default vert, then patch cable, then the three
audio-visualization pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: All 8 pipelines render correctly on Linux under wgpu, judged self-consistently (no artifacts, correct geometry/order/color relationships) rather than against a macOS reference; WIDGET_SHADER_PREAMBLE equivalent verified before widget shaders land; deterministic whole-frame captures produced and committed for the fixed scene set so the macOS comparison can run later. title: hot_reload relative_load test collides on a fixed /tmp path under parallel test threads
description:
Found 2026-08-23 during a Linux full-suite run.

hot_reload::tests::relative_load_falls_back_to_installed_content_roots FAILS under a parallel 'cargo test' run and PASSES when run alone with --test-threads=1. The assertion:

  left:  "/tmp/eseqlisp-load-fallback-elsewhere/scripts/demo-seq.lisp"
  right: "/tmp/eseqlisp-load-fallback-46017/scripts/demo-seq.lisp"

The right-hand path is PID-suffixed; the left-hand one is a fixed literal ('-elsewhere'). So at least one sibling test in crates/eseqlisp/src/hot_reload.rs writes to a hardcoded /tmp directory that a concurrently-running test also reads, and the two interleave.

This is a test-isolation defect, not a Linux port defect -- it would race on macOS too, and is probably masked there because the project's documented runner is 'cargo nextest run', which gives each test its own process. It only became visible here because cargo-nextest is not installed on the Linux box (see the sibling tooling bead).

FIX: give every hot_reload test a unique temp directory (PID + test name, or a tempdir crate handle that cleans up), and remove the fixed '-elsewhere' literal. While in there, grep the rest of crates/eseqlisp for other hardcoded /tmp literals in tests -- the patcher tests already use PID-suffixed names like /tmp/encapsulate-in-macro-<n>.lisp, so the convention exists and this one just missed it.

Related: eseq-tuw is the same CLASS of bug (process-global ACTIVE_THEME shared across parallel tests) and was the other artifact in the same run -- widget_render::waveform::tests::tui_render_highlights_the_active_slice_marker also failed in parallel and passed alone.
acceptance_criteria: hot_reload tests use per-test unique temp paths with no fixed /tmp literals; the named test passes both in isolation and in a full parallel 'cargo test -p eseqlisp' run repeated 3 times; a grep for hardcoded '/tmp/eseqlisp-' literals in crates/eseqlisp tests returns only PID- or nonce-suffixed constructions

title: [macOS host] Verification riders sweep: darwin cargo check, clipping tests, macOS frame times
description:
REQUIRES A MACOS MACHINE. A batching bead: four separate beads each carry one
small macOS-only verification clause. Rather than stranding four Linux beads
on a host they cannot reach, each keeps its Linux-verifiable acceptance and
hands its macOS rider here, so one Mac session clears all of them.

Pull the pushed eseq-linux branch and run:

  1. From eseq-linux.22 -- `cargo check` clean on x86_64-apple-darwin (and
     aarch64-apple-darwin if that is the real target; .22 names x86_64, which
     is worth double-checking against what you actually ship, since the
     vendored DGenLisp is arm64). Cross-checking darwin from Linux needs the
     macOS SDK, which is why it cannot be done on the worker host.
  2. From eseq-linux.17 -- the existing macOS clipping tests still pass after
     the scissor/clip math is shared with ui::gpu_geometry.
  3. From eseq-linux.13 -- macOS frame time with SDF lighting on vs forced
     flat. The Linux/UHD 620 half is measured by the worker; this supplies the
     macOS half of that comparison.
  4. From eseq-linux.12 -- confirm the macOS-gated tests the worker triaged
     are genuinely macOS-only and still pass on a Mac, rather than having been
     gated to hide a real cross-platform failure. This is the one with actual
     judgement in it -- a test gated `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` during a
     port is exactly where a genuine bug gets quietly buried.

Item 4 is the reason this bead is worth doing rather than skipping. Items 1-3
are mechanical.

Do not start until the depended-on beads have landed their Linux halves;
otherwise there is nothing to verify.
